messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: spike in PagerDuty pages for service=redwood-runtime (burst of 180 pages in 10m). Auto-escalation paused? :exclamation:

pagerduty-bot: Triggered PD incident INC-87432 for service: redwood-runtime. Escalation policy: oncall-inference.

Sam K: seeing the flood now — most pages are duplicates, same stack (kv-cache error) from the same host pool. paging every 5s.

Maria L: confirmed. Console graph shows 1s spikes of error-rate from gpu-pool-7 across 12 pods. Likely a transient deploy + client retry storm.

Liam R: are customers impacted? Any 5xx traces in frontend?

Arjun S: quick grep of traces shows increased latency but <1% 5xx. Most failures are internal retried falls back to smaller model. Customer-facing failures minimal.

Sam K: ok so low customer impact but high noise. Goal: reduce PD pages immediately without suppressing real incidents. Propose temporary dedupe + short squelch window and route alerts to #incidents for review.

Maria L: +1. Steps I can take now: 1) enable PD dedupe (group_by: error_signature, host) 2) increase alert throttle to 5m 3) create temp SLO ticket. Want me to apply?

Liam R: do it. While still keep a single page for unique error_signature. We don't want to swallow a genuine new error.

Maria L: applying change to Alertmanager rules now. Patch snippet: ```yaml
    - name: runtime_errors
      match: {service: "redwood-runtime"}
      group_by: ["error_signature","model_version"]
      group_wait: 30s
      group_interval: 5m
      repeat_interval: 15m
```

ops-bot: Alertmanager config update applied to cluster inference-prod: /etc/alertmanager/config.d/runtime-dedupe.yml (dry-run ok).

Sam K: deploying a short PD throttling rule too — PD API call to set auto-resolve delay and limit notifications. Command: ```bash
curl -X PUT "https://api.pagerduty.com/services/PID" \
  -H "Authorization: Token token=$PD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": {"incident_urgency_rule": {"type":"constant","urgency":"low"}}}'
```

Arjun S: careful — changing urgency affects escalation. We should instead add an integration-level suppression for matching incidents. PD support suggested temporary rate limit via event rules.

Maria L: set an event rule: suppress duplicate incidents with the same error_signature for 10m. PD API snippet: ```json
{"event_rule": {"type":"suppress","conditions": [{"field":"body.error_signature","operator":"equals"}],"duration":600}}
```

pagerduty-bot: Event rule applied: suppress duplicates by body.error_signature for 10m.

Liam R: nice — that should collapse the noise. Next: add a dedicated dashboard for 'alert-churn' and a metric to track pages suppressed. Maria can you cook up a quick grafana panel?

Maria L: on it. Panel will show: pages/min, unique signatures/min, suppressed/min, customer-facing 5xx%. Query I'll add: `sum(increase(pd_pages_total[5m])) by (signature)` and `increase(pd_pages_suppressed_total[5m])`

Sam K: also put an automation: if suppressed_pages > 50 in 10m AND 5xx_rate < 0.5%, move alert to non-paging channel and open a ticket. That way we don't lose root cause tracking.

Arjun S: agree. I can add a small lambda that listens to the PD webhook, evaluates conditions, and posts to #incidents with recommended action. Pseudocode: ```python
if suppressed > 50 and error_5xx < 0.5:
  post('#incidents', 'Noise detected — moved to channelless alerting. Run RCA.')
```

Sam K: handoff to next oncall in 30m: @Liam_R you're up for follow-up. Please validate suppression didn't mask anything new and keep the dashboard open.

Liam R: got it. I'll monitor for 2 hours and escalate if anything deviates. Also will open a ticket to revisit group_by keys — maybe use model_version + region instead of host to avoid coupling to autoscaling churn.

Maria L: created ticket INF-4621: review runtime alert grouping and thresholds. Assigned to eng-sre.

ops-bot: Incident INC-87432 updated: status=investigating -> monitoring. Pages suppressed: 162 in last 30m. Customer impact: low. Handoff: Liam R.

Sam K: thanks team. Postmortem follow-ups: (1) implement dedupe rules permanently with sensible group_by, (2) add suppressed_pages metric to standard dashboards, (3) add runbook entry for temporary PD event rules. I'll create the retrospective doc later. :memo:
